classification.difficultyReason: Identify each cross-section, calculate its composite area and exposed perimeter, and substitute into the supplied formula. Curved boundaries and cut faces require distinguishing external perimeter from internal joins.

Surface area of any solid with uniform cross-section

spec.description: Illustrative uniform-cross-section prism with a compound straight-and-curved end. Blue area, red perimeter and green longitudinal edge correspond to B, p and h.
spec.mathematics: The front end area is B, its complete boundary has perimeter p, and the longitudinal extrusion length is h. No numerical dimensions are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent explanatory figure; contains no numerical answer.

spec.description: Trapezoidal prism with parallel vertical cross-section sides 3 m and 7 m, perpendicular separation 3 m, sloping edge 5 m and longitudinal length 6 m.
spec.mathematics: Cross-section area is (3+7)×3/2; its perimeter is 3+7+3+5. Both bottom cross-section corners are right angles.

spec.description: Pentagonal house-shaped prism. Rectangle width 10 m, wall height 5 m, mutually perpendicular roof edges 6 m and 8 m, prism length 15 m.
spec.mathematics: Roof triangle is a 6–8–10 right triangle. The right-angle marker belongs between the 6 m and 8 m roof edges.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens and roof right-angle marker only.

spec.description: Rectangular prism topped by a semicylinder. End profile is a 20 m by 15 m rectangle topped by a semicircle of diameter 20 m; extrusion length 40 m.
spec.mathematics: Radius is 10 m. The rectangle–semicircle join is internal and is excluded from the cross-sectional perimeter.

spec.description: L-shaped prism with overall cross-section width 8.5 and height 10.2, upright width 3.3, lower arm height 2.7 and depth 9.4. Four source right-angle markers retained.
spec.mathematics: L-shaped cross-section is the union of an 8.5 by 2.7 rectangle and a 3.3 by 7.5 rectangle. Dimensions are interpreted as centimetres from the supplied answer.

spec.description: Prism whose end profile comprises an isosceles right triangle above a semicircle. Triangle legs both marked equal, one labelled 15; internal diameter labelled 21.2; extrusion length 35.
spec.mathematics: Use the supplied rounded diameter 21.2, giving r = 10.6. The triangle has perpendicular equal legs 15. The shared diameter is internal.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens, equality ticks and right-angle marker only.

answer.worked:
Use the supplied diameter $21.2\text{ cm}$ for the semicircle.
$$\begin{aligned}r&=21.2\div2=10.6\text{ cm}\\B&=\frac12(15)(15)+\frac12\pi(10.6)^2\\B&=112.5+56.18\pi\text{ cm}^2\\p&=15+15+\pi(10.6)\\p&=30+10.6\pi\text{ cm}\\SA&=2(112.5+56.18\pi)+(30+10.6\pi)(35)\\SA&=1275+483.36\pi\approx2793.5\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Three-quarter cylinder with a longitudinal quarter-sector removed. Radius 2, length 28; two exposed radial cut faces and a right-angle marker at the removed sector.
spec.mathematics: End area is three quarters of a circle. Exposed cross-sectional perimeter consists of a 270-degree arc plus two radii.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens and cut-sector right-angle marker only.

answer.worked:
Include both exposed rectangular cut faces in the perimeter term.
$$\begin{aligned}B&=\frac34\pi(2)^2=3\pi\text{ cm}^2\\p&=\frac34\times2\pi(2)+2+2\\p&=3\pi+4\text{ cm}\\SA&=2(3\pi)+(3\pi+4)(28)\\SA&=112+90\pi\\SA&\approx394.7\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$$

inlines.text: Calculate the surface area of these solids using the formula. Answer to 1 d.p. where needed.
